anchor: that cynosure he had previously been
note: Cynosure: the center of everyone’s attention. Billy was admired on merchant ships but is less noticed on a big warship.

anchor: minor ship’s companies of the merchant marine
note: Merchant marine: the civilian ships that carry cargo, as opposed to the navy’s warships.
Adolescent: of a young person between childhood and adulthood.
Factitious: artificial, produced by society rather than nature. Billy has little experience of such life.

anchor: had there been any conceit or vanity
note: Conceit: too high an opinion of oneself.

anchor: more signally susceptive of that air
note: Signally: markedly, to a noticeable degree. Susceptive: able to take on an impression.

anchor: a rustic beauty transplanted from the provinces
note: Rustic: of the countryside. The comparison is to a country girl brought to a fashionable court.

anchor: the highborn dames of the court
note: Dames: ladies of rank and title, the women of the court.

anchor: the Saxon strain would seem not at all to partake
note: The Anglo-Saxons and the Normans were the two peoples blended in the English. Melville imagines a purely Saxon line.

anchor: the Greek sculptor in some instances gave to his heroic strong man, Hercules
note: Hercules was the Greek hero of great strength. Greek and Roman sculptors often showed him calm and good-natured as well as powerful.

anchor: the indurated hand dyed to the orange-tawny of the toucan’s bill
note: Indurated: hardened. Tawny: a yellowish brown. A toucan is a tropical bird with a large orange bill.

anchor: a hand telling alike of the halyards and tar-bucket
note: Halyards are ropes that hoist sails. Sailors handled tarred rope, so their hands were stained.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Halliards”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

note: Mustered: officially enrolled and counted.
Brisk: quick and lively in manner, here the little officer.

anchor: found in a pretty silklined basket hanging one morning from the knocker of a good man’s door in Bristol
note: Bristol is a large port city in the west of England. Foundlings were often left on the doorsteps of respectable houses.
By-blow: an illegitimate child, born outside marriage.

anchor: Noble descent was as evident in him as in a blood horse
note: Blood horse: a thoroughbred, a horse of pure breeding. Melville says Billy’s good birth shows in his looks.
Jesus tells his disciples, “Be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.” Billy has neither the serpent’s wisdom nor quite the dove’s innocence.
source: The Bible (King James Version), Matthew 10:16, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10

note: The fruit of the tree of knowledge of good and evil in Eden, which Adam and Eve ate against God’s command.
source: The Bible (King James Version), Genesis 3:6, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10

note: Illiterate: unable to read or write. Billy cannot read but makes up songs, as a nightingale sings without being taught.

anchor: a dog of Saint Bernard’s breed
note: The Saint Bernard is a large Swiss dog bred to rescue travelers in the Alps. It is known for gentleness.
Terraqueous: made up of land and water. Melville uses it for the earth, a mock-learned phrase.
Doxies: women of loose morals. Tapsters: those who tap kegs and serve drinks.
Fiddlers’ green: a sailors’ name for a place on shore with drink, music, and women, or for their imagined paradise.
Unsophisticated: simple and natural. Obliquities: departures from what is right.

anchor: exuberance of vitality after long constraint
note: Exuberance: overflowing energy and high spirits, here sailors let loose after long constraint.
Barbarian: here, a man of simple natural ways, not made soft or crooked by civilization.

anchor: ere the urbane Serpent wriggled himself into his company
note: In Genesis, the serpent tempts Eve to eat the forbidden fruit and brings sin into the world.
source: The Bible (King James Version), Genesis 3:1, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10

note: The Christian teaching that all people fell from innocence through the sin of Adam and Eve in Eden.
source: The Bible (King James Version), Genesis 3:6, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10

anchor: prior to Cain’s city and citified man
note: After killing Abel, Cain founded the first city, which Melville treats as the start of civilization and its corruption.
source: The Bible (King James Version), Genesis 4:17, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10

note: Unvitiated: not spoiled or corrupted.
Kaspar Hauser appeared in the streets of Nuremberg in 1828, a bewildered youth who seemed to have lived in isolation and who became a European mystery.

anchor: an occasional liability to a vocal defect
note: Billy sometimes stutters badly when he feels something strongly.
Organic: of the body’s own structure, so not from nervousness alone.
Marplot: someone who spoils a plan by meddling. Here it means the Devil, who spoiled Eden.
Romance: here, a story of adventure and idealized heroes. Melville warns that his tale will be plainer and grimmer.
